# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 9 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**9:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have opened my ear to wonderful mysteries.

**9:2** And You have not closed my ear against the chastisement of [...] the disturbances of the age.

**9:3** For the spirit of flesh [...] in the deeds of wickedness and transgression.

**9:4** I have clung to Your covenant. And the truth that [...] You have set in my heart.

**9:5** And Your covenant-faithfulness for the saving of my soul, and the steps of my foot You have strengthened.

**9:6** Against the dominion of wickedness. And You have made me a trap for transgressors.

**9:7** But healing for all who repent of transgression, and prudence for the simple.

**9:8** And a firm purpose for all the fearful of heart. You have set me as a reproach and derision for the treacherous.

**9:9** A counsel of truth and understanding for the upright of way.

**9:10** Against the devices of the wicked I have become as one whom [...] revile.

**9:11** Through me You have illuminated the faces of the Many; You have magnified Yourself beyond number.

**9:12** For You have made known to me Your wonderful mysteries.

**9:13** And in Your wonderful secret counsel You have shown Your might with me.

**9:14** Doing wonders before the Many for the sake of Your glory.

**9:15** And making known Your mighty deeds to all the living.

**9:16** What is flesh that You should do thus with it? And how is a thing formed of clay able to do great wonders?

**9:17** For he is in iniquity from the womb, and in guilty unfaithfulness until old age.

**9:18** And I know that righteousness belongs not to a man, nor a perfect way to a son of man.

**9:19** To God Most High belong all the deeds of righteousness, and the way of a man is not established.

**9:20** Except by the spirit that God fashioned for him, to make perfect a way for the sons of man.

**9:21** That all His works may know the might of His power and the abundance of His mercies.

**9:22** Upon all the children of His good-pleasure.

**9:23** And trembling and terror have seized me, and all my bones are broken.

**9:24** And my heart melts like wax before the fire, and my knees go as water poured on a slope.

**9:25** For I have remembered my guilty deeds together with the unfaithfulness of my fathers.

**9:26** When the wicked rose against Your covenant and the wretched against Your word.

**9:27** And I said, for my transgression I have been forsaken from Your covenant.

**9:28** But when I remembered the strength of Your hand together with the abundance of Your mercies.

**9:29** I rose and stood, and my spirit held firm in its stand before affliction.

**9:30** For I leaned upon Your covenant-faithfulness and upon the abundance of Your compassion.

**9:31** For You atone for iniquity and purify man by Your righteousness from [...] transgression.

**9:32** Not for man's sake but for Your glory. For You have created the righteous and the wicked.

**9:33** And You have established the spirit of [...] and the purpose of [...] from before the ages.

**9:34** And the judgment of all and the service of [...] You have assigned in all their generations.

**9:35** Doing wonders before the Many for the sake of Your glory and making known Your mighty deeds.

**9:36** To all the living, that all may know Your power and the abundance of Your mercies upon all the children of Your good-pleasure.

**9:37** And I, Your servant, have known by the spirit which You have given me that Your words are truth, and all Your deeds are righteousness.

---

*EMET notes: Column 9 is a rich hymn combining personal testimony with communal theology. "The Many" (ha-rabbim, 9:11, 14, 35) is the Qumran community's self-designation. "Illuminated the faces of the Many" (9:11) is a remarkable claim. The anthropological pessimism of 9:16-19 anticipates Pauline hamartiology. The closing verse (9:37) is one of the most personal statements in 1QH.*
